views.name: qualifying_rows_clean_q_times
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  qualifyId,
  raceId,
  driverId,
  constructorId,
  number,
  position,
  q1,
  CASE
    WHEN q1 IS NULL OR trim(q1) = '' THEN NULL
    -- format M:SS.mmm or MM:SS.mmm or SSS.mmm (no colon) or 1:23.456
    WHEN instr(q1, ':') > 0 THEN
      (CAST(substr(q1, 1, instr(q1, ':')-1) AS INTEGER) * 60 * 1000)
      + (CAST(substr(q1, instr(q1, ':')+1, instr(q1, '.') - instr(q1, ':') -1) AS INTEGER) * 1000)
      + (CAST(substr(q1, instr(q1, '.')+1) AS INTEGER))
    ELSE
      -- no colon: treat as seconds.milliseconds or milliseconds integer
      CASE
        WHEN instr(q1, '.') > 0 THEN
          (CAST(substr(q1, 1, instr(q1, '.')-1) AS INTEGER) * 1000)
          + (CAST(substr(q1, instr(q1, '.')+1) AS INTEGER))
        ELSE
          -- pure integer treat as milliseconds
          CAST(q1 AS INTEGER)
      END
  END AS q1_millis,
  q2,
  CASE
    WHEN q2 IS NULL OR trim(q2) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(q2, ':') > 0 THEN
      (CAST(substr(q2, 1, instr(q2, ':')-1) AS INTEGER) * 60 * 1000)
      + (CAST(substr(q2, instr(q2, ':')+1, instr(q2, '.') - instr(q2, ':') -1) AS INTEGER) * 1000)
      + (CAST(substr(q2, instr(q2, '.')+1) AS INTEGER))
    ELSE
      CASE
        WHEN instr(q2, '.') > 0 THEN
          (CAST(substr(q2, 1, instr(q2, '.')-1) AS INTEGER) * 1000)
          + (CAST(substr(q2, instr(q2, '.')+1) AS INTEGER))
        ELSE
          CAST(q2 AS INTEGER)
      END
  END AS q2_millis,
  q3,
  CASE
    WHEN q3 IS NULL OR trim(q3) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(q3, ':') > 0 THEN
      (CAST(substr(q3, 1, instr(q3, ':')-1) AS INTEGER) * 60 * 1000)
      + (CAST(substr(q3, instr(q3, ':')+1, instr(q3, '.') - instr(q3, ':') -1) AS INTEGER) * 1000)
      + (CAST(substr(q3, instr(q3, '.')+1) AS INTEGER))
    ELSE
      CASE
        WHEN instr(q3, '.') > 0 THEN
          (CAST(substr(q3, 1, instr(q3, '.')-1) AS INTEGER) * 1000)
          + (CAST(substr(q3, instr(q3, '.')+1) AS INTEGER))
        ELSE
          CAST(q3 AS INTEGER)
      END
  END AS q3_millis
FROM qualifying
views.description: Each qualifying row with parsed Q1/Q2/Q3 times converted to milliseconds and basic null canonicalization; keeps original ids to join to drivers/races/constructors.

views.name: lap_time_text_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt.raceId AS raceId,
  lt.driverId AS driverId,
  lt.lap AS lap,
  lt.time AS time,
  -- canonicalize textual time to M:SS.mmm or MM:SS if no milliseconds present in text.
  -- Strategy:
  -- 1) If time is NULL or empty, keep NULL.
  -- 2) If time contains ':' count segments. Common forms:
  --    a) "M:SS.mmm" or "MM:SS.mmm" -> keep minutes:seconds (drop milliseconds after dot for canonical text)
  --    b) "0:MM:SS.mmm" (unexpected extra leading 0) -> drop leading zero segment to produce M:SS...
  --    c) "+5.478" or "+5" (gap notation) -> leave as-is (no colon) but normalize leading '+' removed and prefixed with '+' kept
  -- For portability in SQLite without custom funcs, handle by splitting on ':' using instr and substr.
  CASE
    WHEN lt.time IS NULL OR trim(lt.time) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(lt.time, ':') = 0 THEN
      -- no colon: return trimmed original (e.g., "+5.478" or "5.478")
      trim(lt.time)
    ELSE
      -- has colon(s). We attempt to extract last two colon-separated segments as minutes:seconds(.millis)
      -- Find last colon position by searching for ':' from end via length tricks
      -- pos_last_colon = length - instr(reverse(time), ':') + 1  -- emulate reverse by using substr
      -- SQLite lacks reverse; emulate reverse-instr using iterative approach:
      -- compute index of last colon:
      ( 
        -- compute position of last colon
        CASE
          WHEN instr(lt.time, ':') = 0 THEN trim(lt.time)
          ELSE
            (
              -- position of last colon:
              -- length - instr(substr(time, 1, length-0) reversed) +1
              -- emulate reverse by searching for ':' in progressively shorter suffixes:
              -- We'll extract minutes and seconds by:
              -- seconds_part = substring after last colon
              -- minutes_part = substring before last colon; if that minutes_part itself contains colon and equals '0' (leading extra), drop its leading "0:".
              -- Implementation:
              -- seconds_part:
              substr(lt.time, 
                (length(lt.time) - instr(replace(lt.time, ':', char(1)), char(1)) + 2)
                )
            )
        END
      )
  END AS canonical_time_text,
  lt.milliseconds AS milliseconds
FROM lapTimes lt
views.description: Normalized textual lap times, parsing common variants so M:SS and 0:M:SS can be compared. One row per (raceId, driverId, lap) with both original time and a canonicalized text form (m:ss or mm:ss) to help equality/LIKE comparisons.

views.name: results_with_canonical_fastestlap_speed
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  results.resultId AS resultId,
  results.raceId AS raceId,
  results.driverId AS driverId,
  results.constructorId AS constructorId,
  results.fastestLapSpeed AS fastestLapSpeed_raw,
  CASE
    WHEN trim(results.fastestLapSpeed) = '' THEN NULL
    -- handle speeds like '218.300' or with commas
    WHEN instr(results.fastestLapSpeed, ',') > 0 THEN
      NULLIF(replace(results.fastestLapSpeed, ',', ''), '') * 1.0
    ELSE
      NULLIF(results.fastestLapSpeed, '') * 1.0
  END AS fastestLapSpeed_num
FROM results
WHERE results.fastestLapSpeed IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalize fastestLapSpeed into a numeric measure and expose result-level columns needed for filtering and joins. Keeps one row per results.resultId.

views.name: results_with_driver_nation
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.resultId,
  r.raceId,
  r.driverId,
  d.nationality,
  r.fastestLapSpeed AS fastestLapSpeed_raw,
  CASE
    WHEN r.fastestLapSpeed IS NULL THEN NULL
    -- remove any non-digit/non-dot characters and cast to numeric
    ELSE CAST(
      -- translate commas to dots, then strip any characters except digits and dot
      -- using nested REPLACE to handle common separators
      (CASE
         WHEN instr(replace(replace(r.fastestLapSpeed, ',', '.'), ' ', ''), '.') = 0
         THEN replace(replace(r.fastestLapSpeed, ',', '.'), ' ', '')
         ELSE replace(replace(r.fastestLapSpeed, ',', '.'), ' ', '')
       END)
      AS REAL)
  END AS fastestLapSpeed_num
FROM
  results r
JOIN
  drivers d ON d.driverId = r.driverId
WHERE
  r.fastestLapSpeed IS NOT NULL
views.description: Denormalized result rows joined to driver nationality to allow quick retrieval of driver attributes for a given result. One row per results.resultId.

views.name: race_results_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.resultId,
  r.raceId,
  r.driverId,
  r.constructorId,
  r.fastestLapSpeed,
  -- normalize numeric fastest lap speed: try to cast raw text to number; if NULL keep NULL
  CASE
    WHEN r.fastestLapSpeed IS NULL THEN NULL
    -- remove any non-digit/non-dot characters by keeping digits, dot and comma then replace comma with dot
    WHEN instr(r.fastestLapSpeed, ',') > 0 THEN
      -- replace comma with dot and attempt numeric cast
      CAST(replace(r.fastestLapSpeed, ',', '.') AS REAL)
    ELSE
      CAST(r.fastestLapSpeed AS REAL)
  END AS fastestLapSpeed_num,
  r.position,
  r.points,
  r.statusId
FROM results AS r
views.description: One row per race result (driver in a race) with raw fastest lap speed and other identifying fields for comparisons and joins to drivers/races/constructors.

  dob,
  driverRef,
  code,
  url
FROM drivers
views.description: One row per driver with canonical full name and demographic attributes.

views.name: driver_standings_rows_44
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  driverStandingsId,
  raceId,
  driverId,
  points,
  position,
  positionText,
  wins
FROM driverStandings
views.description: Row-level driver standings entries (one row per driverStandings record) exposing points and wins and linking to driverId and raceId.

views.name: driver_wins_aggregate_by_driver
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  driverId,
  SUM(COALESCE(wins,0)) AS total_wins,
  MAX(points) AS max_points,
  COUNT(*) AS standings_row_count
FROM driverStandings
GROUP BY driverId
views.description: Aggregated driver-level standing measures: total wins and maximum points observed across driverStandings rows for each driver.

views.name: driver_age_calculable
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.driverId,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.dob,
  CAST((strftime('%Y', 'now') - strftime('%Y', d.dob)) - (strftime('%m-%d', 'now') < strftime('%m-%d', d.dob)) AS INTEGER) AS age_years,
  d.nationality
FROM drivers d
WHERE d.dob IS NOT NULL
views.description: Per-driver precomputed age in years (integer) as of current date, plus core identity columns. Aggregation here is per driver (no further grouping); intended to avoid repeating age calculation logic.

views.name: circuits_rowlevel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  circuitId,
  circuitRef,
  name,
  location,
  country,
  lat,
  lng,
  alt
FROM
  circuits
views.description: Row-level circuits with identifying and location attributes. Useful for joining to races to get circuit name, location and country.

views.name: race_with_circuit_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  races.raceId AS raceId,
  races.name AS "races.name",
  races.date AS date,
  races.circuitId AS circuitId,
  circuits.name AS "circuits.name",
  circuits.location AS "circuits.location"
FROM races
LEFT JOIN circuits ON races.circuitId = circuits.circuitId
views.description: Denormalized race rows with their circuit attributes (race-level grain). Exposes all race columns plus circuit name/location for easy filtering and projection.

views.name: drivers_core_49
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  driverId AS "drivers.driverId",
  driverRef AS "drivers.driverRef",
  forename AS "drivers.forename",
  surname AS "drivers.surname",
  number AS "drivers.number",
  code AS "drivers.code",
  nationality AS "drivers.nationality",
  dob AS "drivers.dob"
FROM drivers
views.description: One row per driver with canonical identity and name fields for joining and filtering drivers.

views.name: races_core_50
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  races.raceId AS "races.raceId",
  races.name AS "races.name",
  races.date AS "races.date",
  races.year AS "races.year",
  races.round AS "races.round",
  races.circuitId AS "races.circuitId"
FROM races
views.description: One row per race with key identifying attributes (date, name, season/year, round) for reporting and ordering.

views.name: results_by_race_driver
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  results.resultId AS "results.resultId",
  results.raceId AS "results.raceId",
  results.driverId AS "results.driverId",
  results.constructorId AS "results.constructorId",
  results.position AS "results.position",
  results.positionText AS "results.positionText",
  results.positionOrder AS "results.positionOrder",
  results.points AS "results.points",
  results.time AS "results.time",
  results.milliseconds AS "results.milliseconds",
  results.statusId AS "results.statusId"
FROM results
WHERE results.position IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per race-result (each driver's result in a race), denormalized with driver and race keys and core result measures (position, points, time, status). Useful for filtering by driver and position and joining to races/drivers.

views.name: results_by_driver_race
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.raceId,
  r.driverId,
  r.constructorId,
  r.number,
  r.grid,
  r.position,
  r.positionText,
  r.positionOrder,
  r.points,
  r.laps,
  r.time,
  r.milliseconds,
  r.statusId,
  r.fastestLap,
  r.fastestLapTime,
  r.fastestLapSpeed
FROM results r
views.description: Denormalized results rows at driver-race level: one row per (raceId, driverId) with race and result measures (points, position, status). Useful to find a driver's participation and points in specific races.

views.name: races_core_53
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  races.raceId AS raceId,
  races.name AS name,
  races.year AS year,
  races.circuitId AS circuitId,
  circuits.location AS location,
  circuits.country AS country,
  races.date AS date
FROM races
LEFT JOIN circuits ON races.circuitId = circuits.circuitId
views.description: One row per race with key identifying columns and common descriptive attributes (exposes race identity, name, year, circuit and location fields to support filtering and grouping).
